title: Confidential Information and Unauthorized Disclosure
definition: A secrecy violation occurs when a person discloses, shares, forwards, provides access to, or improperly handles confidential, restricted, proprietary, material non-public, or otherwise protected company information without appropriate authorization. The violation concerns actual unauthorized handling, access, disclosure, or attempted disclosure of protected information.
violations: Disclosing confidential or restricted company information to an unauthorized recipient
Sharing confidential documents, files, business information, financial information, or protected data with an unauthorized person
Forwarding or providing access to protected company information without authorization
Improperly handling protected information in a way that exposes it to unauthorized individuals
Requesting or encouraging another person to disclose protected information without authorization
Sending protected information through an unauthorized channel when this exposes it to an unauthorized recipient
Discussing protected information with a person who does not have a legitimate business need or authorization
Providing confidential or material non-public information to an external party without appropriate authorization
exceptions: Legitimate instructions to keep information confidential
Instructions preventing disclosure until an agreement, contract, or authorization is formally completed
Disclosure explicitly authorized by the appropriate company authority
Sharing information with an explicitly authorized recipient
Routine business communication that does not disclose protected information
Legitimate confidentiality agreements or contract communications that do not themselves disclose protected information
examples: Sending confidential company information to an unauthorized external recipient
Forwarding restricted information to an unauthorized person
Providing an unauthorized person access to confidential files
Sending protected information to a personal account where the recipient is unauthorized
Telling someone not to disclose an agreement until it is signed is not itself a secrecy violation
Discussing a confidentiality agreement without revealing protected information is not itself a secrecy violation

title: Artificial or Misleading Market Activity
definition: A market manipulation or misconduct violation occurs when a person intentionally creates, communicates, coordinates, spreads, or facilitates false, misleading, deceptive, or artificial information or activity intended or reasonably expected to influence investors, market participants, trading activity, market perception, price, supply, or demand. The violation may occur at the planning, proposal, coordination, instruction, communication, or execution stage.
violations: Creating artificial buying or selling activity to influence a market price
Coordinating transactions to artificially increase or decrease a financial instrument's price
Creating false or misleading market activity to influence market participants
Spreading false or misleading information to influence trading activity or market prices
Communicating materially false or misleading information about financial condition, performance, prospects, or business position in a manner capable of influencing investors or market perception
Using deceptive transactions or trading strategies to create a false impression of demand or supply
Encouraging another person to participate in activity intended to artificially influence market conditions
Planning or coordinating activity around an announcement to produce a particular artificial market reaction
Coordinating otherwise legitimate-looking activity where the stated or implied purpose is an artificial market response
Discussing a planned action specifically because it is expected to make the market react in a desired way
Intentionally altering or communicating material business or financial information to create a misleading impression for investors or market participants
exceptions: Legitimate market analysis without deceptive or artificial activity
Ordinary trading or investment decisions made for legitimate purposes
Accurate communication of publicly available market information
Legitimate discussion of market conditions without instructions or intent to manipulate
Accurate reporting of historical events, investigations, allegations, or publicly known information when the communication itself is not misleading
examples: Coordinating transactions to artificially increase a security's price
Creating misleading trading activity to make demand appear higher than it is
Sharing intentionally false information to influence trading
Planning transactions specifically to create an artificial market price
Providing misleading information about a company's financial health that affects investor perception
Coordinating activity around an announcement because the market is expected to react in a desired way

title: Improper Payments, Gifts, and Benefits
definition: A market bribery violation occurs when a person offers, promises, gives, requests, accepts, arranges, or suggests an improper payment, gift, benefit, favor, advantage, hospitality, or personal benefit with the purpose or expectation of improperly influencing a business, commercial, regulatory, approval, procurement, or market-related decision.
violations: Offering money or another improper benefit in exchange for favorable business treatment
Requesting or accepting an improper payment or benefit to influence a business decision
Offering a gift, favor, service, advantage, hospitality, or personal benefit to improperly influence a decision
Agreeing to provide an improper benefit in return for preferential treatment
Using an intermediary or third party to provide an improper benefit to influence a decision
Arranging an improper payment or benefit to obtain an unfair business advantage
Suggesting that a gift, favor, gesture, payment, or personal benefit could help obtain approval or favorable treatment
Offering or suggesting a personal benefit to a decision maker in connection with obtaining a business approval or favorable outcome
exceptions: Legitimate business expenses permitted by company policy
Ordinary business activities without an attempt to improperly influence a decision
Benefits explicitly permitted and appropriately authorized
Reasonable and authorized business hospitality not intended to influence a decision
examples: Offering money in exchange for awarding a contract
Offering an inappropriate gift to influence a customer's decision
Requesting a personal payment in exchange for approving a transaction
Arranging for another person to provide a benefit for preferential treatment
Suggesting that a small gesture for a decision maker could help obtain approval
Offering a favor to someone responsible for approving a business transaction

title: Unauthorized Communication Channels
definition: A change in communication violation occurs when business-related communication is moved, continued, redirected, or intentionally invited from an approved company communication channel to a personal or external communication channel that is not approved for company business.
violations: Moving a business discussion from an approved channel to a personal or external channel
Asking someone to continue business communication through a personal messaging service
Using an external messaging service to continue discussions concerning company business, agreements, transactions, or work
Redirecting business communication to an external channel to bypass an approved company communication system
Continuing a business discussion through an external communication method
Inviting a business contact to communicate about work through a personal messaging application
Providing a personal messaging account for the purpose of continuing company business outside an approved channel
Suggesting that business communication continue through WhatsApp, personal messaging, personal email, or another external service
exceptions: The external channel is explicitly approved for the relevant business activity
The communication is clearly personal and unrelated to company business
The external channel is specifically authorized by the company
An approved business process requires the external channel
examples: Asking a business contact to continue a company discussion through a personal messaging service
Moving a business agreement discussion to an external messaging application
Asking someone to continue company-related communication through a personal account
Inviting a business contact to continue work outside the approved communication system
Discussing a business agreement and saying 'Feel free to ding me on WhatsApp anytime'

title: Complaint Handling and Reporting
definition: A complaints-related violation occurs when a legitimate complaint, concern, allegation, or report involving employee conduct, business practices, or company processes is improperly ignored, suppressed, mishandled, discouraged, concealed, or intentionally prevented from reaching the appropriate reporting, investigation, compliance, legal, HR, management, or review process.
violations: Preventing a legitimate complaint from being reported through the appropriate process
Ignoring a complaint that requires investigation or appropriate handling
Suppressing or concealing a legitimate complaint or concern
Improperly handling a formal complaint to prevent appropriate review
Discouraging someone from reporting a legitimate concern
Retaliating against or improperly treating a person because they raised a legitimate complaint
Instructing or encouraging someone not to report a legitimate complaint
Preventing a complaint from reaching compliance, HR, legal, management, or another appropriate function
Deliberately delaying or obstructing a complaint investigation for an improper purpose
exceptions: Simply reporting a legitimate concern or complaint in good faith
Routine communication about a complaint that does not suppress or mishandle it
Resolving a complaint through an authorized company process
Requesting information needed to properly investigate a complaint
Directing a complaint to the correct authorized reporting or investigation channel
Describing a historical complaint, lawsuit, investigation, or allegation without suppressing or mishandling it
examples: Telling an employee not to report a legitimate workplace concern
Ignoring a formal complaint requiring investigation
Preventing a complaint from reaching compliance
Suppressing a complaint to avoid investigation
Encouraging someone to keep a legitimate complaint informal so it is not reported

title: Employee Ethical Conduct and Appropriate Workplace Communication
definition: An employee ethics violation occurs when an employee uses official company communication or workplace interactions for inappropriate, unprofessional, personal, social, dishonest, deceptive, or otherwise unacceptable conduct that conflicts with expected workplace behavior. Context must be considered. Legitimate business activities involving meals, drinks, entertainment, hospitality, events, or social interaction are not violations when authorized and relevant to legitimate company activity.
violations: Using official company communication for inappropriate personal or social discussion unrelated to legitimate business activity
Discussing alcohol, drinks, drinking, partying, or similar personal activities in official business communication when unrelated to legitimate business activity
Discussing personal entertainment, social gatherings, running, recreational activities, or similar personal matters in official business communication when inappropriate or unrelated to business
Sending inappropriate personal messages through official company communication
Using company communication for inappropriate personal arrangements or requests
Engaging in inappropriate, unprofessional, disrespectful, dishonest, deceptive, or improper communication
Making inappropriate personal requests, suggestions, or arrangements through official company communication
Using workplace relationships or company communication to facilitate inappropriate personal activities
Using company resources or official communication channels for unauthorized personal purposes
Knowingly providing false or misleading information for an improper purpose
Engaging in dishonest or deceptive conduct related to company business
Intentionally changing, falsifying, concealing, or misrepresenting business information or figures for an improper purpose
Changing figures or reports to make results appear more favorable when the change is misleading or dishonest
Concealing relevant information to obtain an improper benefit
Engaging in an undisclosed or improperly managed conflict of interest
Attempting to conceal inappropriate or improper employee conduct
exceptions: Legitimate business communication
Legitimate company-sponsored social activities
Authorized business entertainment or hospitality
Business-related discussion of meals, drinks, entertainment, or events
Professional communication appropriate to the business context
Clearly personal communication that is not sent through an official company communication channel
Good-faith business decisions
Ordinary mistakes that do not involve improper conduct
Authorized company events or activities
Accurate correction of figures for a legitimate business purpose
Good-faith report preparation that does not misrepresent information
examples: Using official company email to discuss personal drinking or drinks unrelated to business
Discussing personal activities such as running or social plans through an official business email without a legitimate business purpose
Using company email to arrange an inappropriate personal social activity
Sending inappropriate personal messages through official company communication
Changing figures before sharing a report so results appear more favorable
Knowingly altering business figures to create a misleading impression

title: Business Communication Disclaimer
definition: A disclaimer violation occurs when sensitive financial, commercial, transactional, client-related, or otherwise designated business information is distributed or proposed for distribution without a disclaimer or distribution restriction required by the applicable communication policy.
violations: Distributing sensitive financial information without the required disclaimer
Distributing sensitive commercial information without the required disclaimer
Distributing sensitive transactional or client-related information without the required disclaimer
Proposing to distribute sensitive business information without the required disclaimer or distribution restriction
Preparing sensitive business material for distribution to attendees or recipients when the required disclaimer or distribution restriction is absent
Failing to apply a required distribution restriction to sensitive business communication
exceptions: The required disclaimer is already present
The required authorized distribution restriction is already present
The information is not subject to a disclaimer requirement
The communication is clearly outside the scope of sensitive financial, commercial, transactional, or client-related information
Distribution is explicitly authorized without the disclaimer under the applicable company policy
examples: A detailed financial briefing prepared for distribution without the required disclaimer
A sensitive commercial presentation prepared for external recipients without the required distribution restriction
A client-related business document distributed without the required disclaimer
Sensitive financial information proposed for distribution without the required disclaimer
